25	
26	Consider which capability, mode, configuration option, compatibility promise, or
27	combination of features creates most of the complexity. A narrower, explicit
28	contract can remove entire branches of implementation and testing. Name what users
29	would give up and whether anyone currently relies on it. Propose changes to existing
30	product promises; do not silently remove them during a refactor.
31	
32	Distinguish a present requirement from an anticipated one. An extension point,
33	plugin system, alternate transport, or scaling mechanism needs a concrete consumer
34	or constraint. When deferring it, identify what evidence would make it worth adding
35	and whether adding it later would actually be difficult. Preserve inexpensive
36	boundaries that make change easy without implementing every imagined future.
37	
38	For public software, check the supported deployment and client contracts. The
39	maintainers' own deployment is not evidence that other supported modes are unused.
40	An unused internal helper and a published API carry different removal costs.
41	
42	Choose which edge cases deserve machinery
43	
44	Judge a case by its credible trigger, frequency, consequence, and recovery cost.
45	Use actual callers, deployments, incidents, or a concrete execution path. Do not
46	invent numerical probabilities or build recommendations around chains of unlikely
47	coincidences. A merely possible scenario is not automatically worth a new subsystem.
48	
49	Timeouts, restarts, duplicate delivery, and interrupted requests are ordinary
50	conditions in systems that cross process or network boundaries. Data loss,
51	authorization failures, and irreversible side effects can deserve a simple guard
52	even when uncommon. Simplification should preserve the invariants that protect
53	people's work.
54	
55	Often the useful choice is to make a case unsupported or impossible: reject an
56	ambiguous request, require one owner, bound concurrency, or accept a documented
57	limit. Where failure is recoverable and visible, an explicit error and retry may be
58	simpler than automatic repair. Where a failed attempt may already have changed
59	something, retry needs an account of that side effect.
60	
61	Prefer removing a class of failures over adding another special-case handler. Ask
62	what constraint would make the problematic state unreachable.
63	
64	Give the system fewer things to coordinate
65	
66	Look for facts stored in several places, independently updated flags, competing
67	owners, and state that can be derived from an authoritative value. Each copy creates
68	an obligation to synchronize, invalidate, and repair it. A cache may earn that cost
69	through a measured need; otherwise deriving the value can remove the obligation.
70	
71	Consider whether related changes can share one transaction or one owner. Whether a
72	response can carry information that currently requires a callback. Whether one layer
73	can own retries instead of several multiplying them. Whether an existing component
74	can do the job without another service, queue, scheduler, or deployment dependency.
75	These are candidates, not bans: asynchronous work and separate services may satisfy
76	real lifetime, isolation, or throughput requirements.
77	
78	A good boundary hides a coherent responsibility behind a small contract. A boundary
79	that only forwards arguments or renames the same fields may add navigation without
80	reducing what callers need to understand. Judge an abstraction by the detail it
81	removes from its users, not by how many implementations it could support someday.
82	
83	Include operations in the comparison. A design with fewer source files can still
84	require more configuration, credentials, migrations, monitoring, and recovery
85	procedures. Prefer a system whose behavior can be explained from a request through
86	to its durable effects without reconstructing several implicit protocols.
87	
88	Seek elegance in the model and the code
89	
90	Look for a representation that makes the rules obvious. A small set of explicit
91	states may replace interacting booleans. One canonical identity may remove repeated
92	matching and fallback logic. Normalizing input at a real boundary may remove the
93	same defensive checks from every consumer. Preserve validation where trust changes.
94	
95	Prefer ordinary control flow, meaningful names, and cohesive functions. Extract a
96	helper when it gives a concept a useful name or hides detail the caller should not
97	manage. Inline a helper when following it adds more work than reading its body.
98	Neither function length nor file count decides this alone.
99	
100	Share knowledge that must change together. Similar-looking code that represents
101	different policies may be cheaper to keep separate. If a shared abstraction collects
102	mode flags and exceptions for every caller, splitting it can remove more complexity
103	than further generalizing it. Avoid both copied business rules and forced reuse.
104	
105	Look for code whose reason to exist has disappeared: completed rollout branches,
106	obsolete adapters, redundant conversions, and wrappers with no remaining policy.
107	Check consumers and compatibility before recommending deletion. Carry useful tests
108	forward around observable behavior and important invariants; remove tests that only
109	enshrine deleted plumbing. Do not replace removed code with a larger framework or a
110	forest of mocks merely to preserve the old shape.
111	
112	Make the suggestion worth acting on
113	
114	Understand what the current design accomplishes and why it has its present shape
115	before judging it. Ground each recommendation in a specific responsibility,
116	contract, state, or code path. Explain what could disappear, why the remaining
117	system is easier to reason about, and what behavior or tradeoff changes.
118	
119	Prefer a few substantial suggestions to a long list of stylistic nits. Label design
120	alternatives and maintainability improvements as Suggestion (non-blocking).
121	Reserve stronger findings for concrete, significant correctness or reliability
122	problems, with a reachable trigger and impact. Separate demonstrated failures from
123	hypotheses and identify what still needs verification.
124	
125	When reviewing, remain in review mode unless asked to implement. Posting findings
126	requires the user's authorization. When implementing, favor a narrow change whose
127	behavior can be checked over a wholesale rewrite. Consider the cost of migration,
128	compatibility, and temporary coexistence alongside the eventual reduction in code.
129	A cleanup that takes weeks to repay may be less useful than deleting one unnecessary
130	mode today.
131	
132	A useful suggestion might say: "These two status fields describe the same lifecycle
133	but are updated independently. Deriving the badge from the existing status would
134	remove the synchronization effect and its stale-state path. This is appropriate if
135	the badge has no separate lifecycle requirement." It names a deletion and its
136	condition without treating one pattern as universally wrong.

296	+export const INVITE_JOINED_MESSAGE = "You joined a new workspace!"
297	+export const INVITE_ALREADY_JOINED_MESSAGE = "You already joined this workspace."
298	+
299	+const MESSAGE_BY_CODE: Record<string, string> = {
300	+    INVITE_EMAIL_MISMATCH:
301	+        "This invitation is not for you. Sign in with the invited account to accept it.",
302	+    INVITE_EXPIRED: "This invitation has expired. Ask the workspace admin for a new one.",
303	+    INVITE_NOT_FOUND: "This invitation is not valid. Ask the workspace admin for another one.",
304	+}
305	+
306	+const FALLBACK_MESSAGE =
307	+    "This invitation may have expired, is no longer valid, or was sent to a different email address. Please check that you're signed in with the correct account, or request a new invitation from the workspace administrator."
308	+
309	+export interface InviteFailure {
310	+    alreadyAccepted: boolean
311	+    message: string
312	+    /** The request may succeed if sent again; a known invite error will not. */
313	+    retryable: boolean
314	+}
315	+
316	+interface AcceptError {
317	+    response?: {status?: number; data?: {detail?: unknown}}
318	+}
319	+
320	+/** What a failed accept request means for the person. */
321	+export const inviteFailure = (error: unknown): InviteFailure => {
322	+    const response = (error as AcceptError | null)?.response
323	+    const detail = response?.data?.detail
324	+    const code =
325	+        detail && typeof detail === "object" ? (detail as {error?: unknown}).error : undefined
326	+    if (code === "INVITE_ALREADY_ACCEPTED" || (code === undefined && response?.status === 409)) {
327	+        return {alreadyAccepted: true, message: INVITE_ALREADY_JOINED_MESSAGE, retryable: false}
328	+    }
329	+    const known = typeof code === "string" ? MESSAGE_BY_CODE[code] : undefined
330	+    return {
331	+        alreadyAccepted: false,
332	+        message: known ?? FALLBACK_MESSAGE,
333	+        retryable: known === undefined,
334	+    }
335	+}

342	+import type {InviteParams} from "@agenta/auth"
343	+
344	+/** The five values the emailed invite link always carries. */
345	+export type PendingInvite = Required<InviteParams>
346	+
347	+const PENDING_INVITE_KEY = "agenta:mobile:pending-invite"
348	+/** Long enough to sign up and verify an email; the emailed link stays valid for days. */
349	+const PENDING_INVITE_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000
350	+
351	+const isComplete = (invite: InviteParams): invite is PendingInvite =>
352	+    Boolean(
353	+        invite.token &&
354	+        invite.email &&
355	+        invite.organization_id &&
356	+        invite.workspace_id &&
357	+        invite.project_id,
358	+    )
359	+
360	+/** Keeps an invite through sign-in. The trip through `/auth` and a provider drops the query. */
361	+export function rememberInvite(invite: InviteParams, now = Date.now()): void {
362	+    if (!isComplete(invite)) return
363	+    try {
364	+        localStorage.setItem(PENDING_INVITE_KEY, JSON.stringify({invite, capturedAt: now}))
365	+    } catch {
366	+        // storage unavailable (private mode / quota): the person opens the link again after sign-in
367	+    }
368	+}
369	+
370	+/** The kept invite, or null when none is kept or its window has passed. */
371	+export function readPendingInvite(now = Date.now()): PendingInvite | null {
372	+    try {
373	+        const raw = localStorage.getItem(PENDING_INVITE_KEY)
374	+        const parsed = raw
375	+            ? (JSON.parse(raw) as {invite?: InviteParams; capturedAt?: unknown})
376	+            : null
377	+        if (
378	+            parsed?.invite &&
379	+            typeof parsed.capturedAt === "number" &&
380	+            now - parsed.capturedAt <= PENDING_INVITE_TTL_MS &&
381	+            isComplete(parsed.invite)
382	+        ) {
383	+            return parsed.invite
384	+        }
385	+        return null
386	+    } catch {
387	+        return null
388	+    }
389	+}
390	+
391	+export function forgetInvite(): void {
392	+    try {
393	+        localStorage.removeItem(PENDING_INVITE_KEY)
394	+    } catch {
395	+        // storage unavailable: nothing was kept
396	+    }
397	+}

463	+/** Accepts the kept invite once a session is confirmed, and owns what the person can do next. */
464	+export const useInviteAccept = () => {
465	+    const router = useRouter()
466	+    const logout = useLogout()

468	+    const startedRef = useRef(false)
469	+    // AuthGate moves a signed-out person to /auth; the invite waits in storage meanwhile.
470	+    const session = useQuery({

472	+        queryFn: () => fetchProjects(),
473	+        staleTime: 30_000,
474	+    })
475	+    const signedIn = session.data !== undefined && session.data.kind !== "unauthenticated"
476	+
477	+    const openProject = useCallback(
478	+        async (invite: PendingInvite, joined: string) => {
479	+            forgetInvite()
480	+            message.success(joined)
481	+            await Promise.all([
482	+                queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey: ["mobile", "projects"]}),
483	+                queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey: ["orgs"]}),
484	+            ])
485	+            const context = {workspaceId: invite.organization_id, projectId: invite.project_id}
486	+            writeLastContext(context)
487	+            const user = await queryClient
488	+                .fetchQuery({queryKey: ["profile"], queryFn: fetchProfile, staleTime: 30_000})
489	+                .catch(() => null)
490	+            if (user?.id && isOnboardingPending(user.id)) {
491	+                markOnboardingInvited(user.id)
492	+                const {workspaceId, projectId} = context
493	+                await router.replace(
494	+                    `/w/${encodeURIComponent(workspaceId)}/p/${encodeURIComponent(projectId)}/onboarding`,
495	+                )

497	+            }

499	+        },
500	+        [router],
501	+    )
502	+
503	+    const accept = useCallback(async () => {
504	+        const invite = readPendingInvite()
505	+        if (!invite) {
506	+            await router.replace("/")
507	+            return
508	+        }
509	+        try {
510	+            await acceptWorkspaceInvite(
511	+                {
512	+                    token: invite.token,
513	+                    email: invite.email,
514	+                    organizationId: invite.organization_id,
515	+                    workspaceId: invite.workspace_id,
516	+                    projectId: invite.project_id,
517	+                },
518	+                true,
519	+            )
520	+        } catch (error) {
521	+            const outcome = inviteFailure(error)
522	+            if (outcome.alreadyAccepted) {
523	+                await openProject(invite, outcome.message)
524	+                return
525	+            }
526	+            setFailure(outcome)
527	+            return
528	+        }
529	+        await openProject(invite, INVITE_JOINED_MESSAGE)

540	+        retry: () => {

543	+        },
544	+        goBack: () => {
545	+            forgetInvite()
546	+            void router.replace("/")
547	+        },
548	+        // The invite stays kept, so signing in with the invited email accepts it.
549	+        switchAccount: () => void logout(),
550	+    }

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Invite link opens /m
The API SHALL build the emailed invite link as `<web_url>/m/auth` with the same five query values as today.

#### Scenario: Invite email is sent
- **WHEN** an owner invites a person
- **THEN** the link is `<web_url>/m/auth?token&email&organization_id&workspace_id&project_id`

### Requirement: Invite survives sign-in
The `/m` sign-in SHALL keep an invite that has a token and an organization id for 30 minutes in browser storage, through every sign-in method.

#### Scenario: Password or one-time code
- **WHEN** a person opens the link and signs in by password or one-time code
- **THEN** `/m` opens the accept screen with the invite values

#### Scenario: Social or SSO
- **WHEN** a person opens the link and signs in through a provider redirect
- **THEN** `/m` opens the accept screen with the invite values after the callback

#### Scenario: Email without a token
- **WHEN** a person opens `/m/auth?email=a@b.c`
- **THEN** `/m` keeps no invite and fills in the email as it does today

#### Scenario: Window passed
- **WHEN** a person finishes sign-in more than 30 minutes after opening the link
- **THEN** `/m` ignores the kept invite and opens the project home

### Requirement: Accept screen outcomes
The `/m/invite` screen SHALL accept the kept invite once and show the outcomes of the old accept page.

#### Scenario: Accepted
- **WHEN** the API accepts the invite
- **THEN** `/m` shows "You joined a new workspace!", clears the invite, refreshes organizations and projects, and opens the invited project

#### Scenario: Already accepted
- **WHEN** the API answers `INVITE_ALREADY_ACCEPTED`
- **THEN** `/m` shows "You already joined this workspace.", clears the invite, and opens the invited project

#### Scenario: Different email
- **WHEN** a signed-in person with another email opens the link and the API answers `INVITE_EMAIL_MISMATCH`
- **THEN** `/m` shows "This invitation is not for you. Sign in with the invited account to accept it." with "Go back to your workspaces" and "Sign in with a different account"

#### Scenario: Switch account
- **WHEN** the person picks "Sign in with a different account" and then signs in with the invited email
- **THEN** `/m` accepts the invite without a new click on the email link

#### Scenario: Go back
- **WHEN** the person picks "Go back to your workspaces"
- **THEN** `/m` clears the invite and opens the root resolver

#### Scenario: Expired or not valid
- **WHEN** the API answers `INVITE_EXPIRED` or `INVITE_NOT_FOUND`
- **THEN** `/m` shows the old page's message for that code on the same card

#### Scenario: Other failure
- **WHEN** the request fails with no known code
- **THEN** `/m` shows the old page's fallback message with a retry control, and keeps the invite

### Requirement: Onboarding for a new invited person
A new account that accepts an invite SHALL answer the onboarding questions only and then open the invited project.

#### Scenario: New person, project has agents
- **WHEN** a new account accepts an invite to a project with agents
- **THEN** `/m` shows the questions, sends `survey sent` after the last one, and opens the project home

#### Scenario: New person, empty project
- **WHEN** a new account accepts an invite to a project with no agents
- **THEN** `/m` shows the same questions and does not show the credits or first agent steps

#### Scenario: Existing person
- **WHEN** an existing account accepts an invite
- **THEN** `/m` shows no questions and opens the invited project

### Requirement: Gates keep invites on /m
The gates SHALL send an invite link to `/m` with its query and SHALL leave password reset links where they work today.

#### Scenario: Old link in an inbox
- **WHEN** anyone opens `/auth?token=t&organization_id=o&...`, including an opted out or Classic mode person
- **THEN** the desktop gate redirects to `/m/auth?token=t&organization_id=o&...`

#### Scenario: Password reset
- **WHEN** anyone opens `/auth/reset-password?token=t&tenantId=public`
- **THEN** the desktop gate passes as it does today

#### Scenario: Classic mode on /m
- **WHEN** a Classic mode person opens `/m/auth` with an invite, or `/m/invite`
- **THEN** the mobile gate passes

### Requirement: Invite link when email is off
The `/m` Members settings SHALL show the invite link the API returns when the deployment has no email service.

#### Scenario: Email is off
- **WHEN** an owner sends an invitation on a deployment with no email service
- **THEN** `/m` shows a dialog with the email, the link, and a Copy button

#### Scenario: Email is on
- **WHEN** an owner sends an invitation and the API returns no link
- **THEN** `/m` closes the invite dialog and shows no link dialog
## Why

Invite emails open the old app. `api/oss/src/services/organization_service.py:139-145` builds `<web_url>/auth?token=...`, `isTokenBearingAuthLink` keeps that link on the old sign-in, and the person accepts on the old `/workspaces/accept` page. `/m` is the main app, and it drops every invite value except `email` during sign-in.

## What Changes

- The API builds the invite link with `/m/auth`.
- The `/m` sign-in keeps the invite in browser storage through password, one-time code, social and SSO sign-in.
- `/m` gets an accept screen at `/m/invite`, with the outcomes of the old page.
- The person lands in the invited project.
- A new invited person answers the onboarding questions only, then opens the invited project.
- The desktop gate forwards an old invite link to `/m/auth` with its query. Password reset links stay where they are.
- The mobile gate does not send an invite away from `/m` for a Classic mode user.
- `/m` Members settings shows the invite link when the deployment has no email service.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `mobile-invites`: joining an organization from an emailed invite link in `/m`.

### Modified Capabilities

None. No existing spec covers invites.

## Impact

- `api/oss/src/services/organization_service.py`: link path only. No API contract change.
- `web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts` and its tests.
- `web/mobile/src/features/invite/` (new), `web/mobile/src/pages/invite/index.tsx` (new), `SignInScreen.tsx`, `ContextResolver.tsx`, `features/onboarding/*`.
- `docs/design/onboarding-revamp/questions-and-survey-parity.md`: the old form no longer sends `survey sent` for invites.
- No change to `web/oss` or `web/ee`, which are abandoned.

# Simplify review

Base: 4a0eae2ea358038dc2d78818bc6dffdc946cfef0
Head: 9acd9c670dea38c1cffd8ca6d131835359da4562

## Findings

### 1. The desktop gate forward serves a 7-day window that the old page already covers
- Severity: Medium
- Where: web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts:352-355 (the forward), web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts:102 (the `isInviteLink` exclusion), web/packages/agenta-shared/tests/unit/mobileGate.test.ts:753 (its test), openspec/changes/invites-on-mobile/specs/mobile-invites/spec.md "Old link in an inbox"
- What is wrong: The API change makes every new link `/m/auth`. So the forward only acts on links emailed before the deploy, and those links expire within 7 days. The settled rule keeps the old `/workspaces/accept` page, and `isDesktopOnlyLink` already keeps an old link on the old sign-in. So without the forward, an old link still works, on the same path it follows today. The code comment "an invite link only ever completes on /m" is not true while the old page exists. The forward also does not help the Helm case in design.md, because the gate runs inside the old web app, and that case has the old web app turned off. The cost is a rule in the shared gate that overrides the opt-out and Classic mode preferences, and a rule that no one can reach after 7 days but that someone must remember to remove. Without the forward, the desktop gate returns to its current behavior and the `isTokenBearingAuthLink` docstring does not need to change.
- Smallest fix: Remove the forward, remove the `isInviteLink` check in `isTokenBearingAuthLink`, and remove the forward test and the spec scenario. Keep `isInviteLink` and `INVITE_ROUTE_RE` in `decideMobileGate`, because new links need them for Classic mode users. Tradeoff: for up to 7 days after the deploy, a person with an old link joins through the old app and answers the old survey form. If Mahmoud wants those people on `/m` as well, keep the forward, correct the comment, and record a date to remove it. Finding 2 still applies in that case.

### 2. The `isInviteLink` check in `isTokenBearingAuthLink` is dead code in either case
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts:102
- What is wrong: `isDesktopOnlyLink` is the only caller of this function, and it has two callers. `decideDesktopGate` returns for an invite link at line 353, before it reaches line 358. `useClassicModeGate.ts` returns for every `/auth` path on the line above its `isDesktopOnlyLink` check. `decideMobileGate` does not call it. So no running path sends an invite link to this check, and no test in `web/packages/agenta-shared/tests`, `web/mobile/tests` or `web/oss/tests` calls these functions by name.
- Smallest fix: Restore line 102 and the old docstring. Behavior does not change.

### 3. `openProject` writes the last context a second time and builds a URL by hand
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:40, web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:46-49
- What is wrong: Both branches of `openProject` end on a `/w/<id>/p/<id>/...` route. `ContextSync` is mounted in `AppProviders` and already calls `writeLastContext` for every such route (ContextSync.tsx:76-80), so line 40 repeats it. The onboarding URL is also written by hand, with a destructure that exists only for that URL, next to the `projectHomeUrl` helper. `lib/context.ts` is where the other project URL helpers live.
- Smallest fix: Delete `writeLastContext` and its import and mock. Add a `projectOnboardingUrl(context)` helper in `lib/context.ts`, and use it here and in `HomeScreen.tsx:83` if that is convenient. One small behavior change: the last context is written after the navigation lands, not before it starts.

### 4. `inviteFailure` models a success as a failure and keeps a fallback the API cannot trigger
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/inviteOutcome.ts:15, web/mobile/src/features/invite/inviteOutcome.ts:31, web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:75-80
- What is wrong: `INVITE_ALREADY_ACCEPTED` is an ordinary success path, because OSS consumes the invite at sign-up. It still returns an `InviteFailure` with `retryable: false`, and the caller then has to branch on `alreadyAccepted` and never reads the other field. The `code === undefined && status === 409` branch is a copy from the old page. The accept handler in `organization_router.py:311-336` always sends a code with its 409, so the branch is a compatibility net for an API that no longer exists.
- Smallest fix: Delete the bare 409 branch and its test line. Check `isInviteAlreadyAccepted(error)` in the catch block, or return a small tagged result, so that `InviteFailure` only has `message` and `retryable`. Separately, the design says every string comes from the old page, but "Try again" is not in `web/oss/src/pages/workspaces/accept.tsx` or in `web/oss/src/components/pages/auth`. Confirm that string with the owner or take it from wherever it was copied.

### 5. The invited mark could be a value on the pending mark
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/onboardingPending.ts:6-7, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/onboardingPending.ts:48-62, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:62
- What is wrong: The invited key only has meaning while the pending key exists, and the code removes them together, so the two keys describe one fact. Nothing reads the value of the pending key today, only whether it exists. A second key gives a state that the code must avoid, which is why the host guards `invited` with `!preview`.
- Smallest fix: Keep one key. Write the value `"invited"` in `markOnboardingInvited`, and compare that value in `isOnboardingInvited`. The second `removeItem` goes away, and `invited` no longer needs the `!preview` guard. A mark is still needed, because the person can leave and come back through Home. This is optional.

### 6. The end of the question flow is inferred from `to === from`, and the deleted draft comes back
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:152-160, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/onboardingRoute.ts (`nextStep`), web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:189-192, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/useDraftSave.ts
- What is wrong: `nextStep` returns the same step at the end of the list. Before this change no question could reach that case, and now that return value is the signal for "finished". `advance` has one caller, so the two-argument shape adds a step for the reader. Also, `reportCompleted` dispatches and then `onQuestionsDone` calls `endOnboarding` in the same tick. The dispatch commits after that, `useDraftSave` queues the new draft, and the timer or the unmount flush writes it back. So the answers stay in localStorage after `endOnboarding` deleted them. I found this by reading the code and did not run it. The effect is small, because the pending mark is gone and only the preview page would read that draft.
- Smallest fix: Have `nextStep` return `undefined` at the end of the list, and branch on that in the question's `onAdvance`. For the draft, the simplest choice is to accept the leftover and say so in a comment. Otherwise give `useDraftSave` a `discard` function that drops the pending save, and call it on this path.

## What to keep

- `ContextResolver` as the single reader of the pending invite. Every sign-in path ends at the root, so this avoids three places to keep in step.
- The localStorage invite with a 30 minute window, written through the existing `onInvite` callback. It has the same shape as `?template=`, and two short copies are cheaper than a shared storage helper for two callers.
- The questions-only path in the existing onboarding flow. The `steps` prop was already there, so filtering it reuses the step guards, the draft, and the analytics, including the `survey sent` check that follows the last shown question. A separate questions screen would copy all of that. The host still loads templates and the model for steps it does not show, and I do not think that is worth another branch.
- Opening onboarding directly from the accept screen. Home dismisses the pending mark when the project has agents, so going through Home would lose the questions in that case.
- `InvitedLinkDialog` as its own small component, and the thin `InviteAcceptScreen` and page shell.
- The one-line API link change.

Rating: Medium

Without the forward, the desktop gate returns to its current behavior and the `isTokenBearingAuthLink` docstring does not need to change.
- Smallest fix: Remove the forward, remove the `isInviteLink` check in `isTokenBearingAuthLink`, and remove the forward test and the spec scenario. Keep `isInviteLink` and `INVITE_ROUTE_RE` in `decideMobileGate`, because new links need them for Classic mode users. Tradeoff: for up to 7 days after the deploy, a person with an old link joins through the old app and answers the old survey form. If Mahmoud wants those people on `/m` as well, keep the forward, correct the comment, and record a date to remove it. Finding 2 still applies in that case.

### 2. The `isInviteLink` check in `isTokenBearingAuthLink` is dead code in either case
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/mobileGate/index.ts:102
- What is wrong: `isDesktopOnlyLink` is the only caller of this function, and it has two callers. `decideDesktopGate` returns for an invite link at line 353, before it reaches line 358. `useClassicModeGate.ts` returns for every `/auth` path on the line above its `isDesktopOnlyLink` check. `decideMobileGate` does not call it. So no running path sends an invite link to this check, and no test in `web/packages/agenta-shared/tests`, `web/mobile/tests` or `web/oss/tests` calls these functions by name.
- Smallest fix: Restore line 102 and the old docstring. Behavior does not change.

### 3. `openProject` writes the last context a second time and builds a URL by hand
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:40, web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:46-49
- What is wrong: Both branches of `openProject` end on a `/w/<id>/p/<id>/...` route. `ContextSync` is mounted in `AppProviders` and already calls `writeLastContext` for every such route (ContextSync.tsx:76-80), so line 40 repeats it. The onboarding URL is also written by hand, with a destructure that exists only for that URL, next to the `projectHomeUrl` helper. `lib/context.ts` is where the other project URL helpers live.
- Smallest fix: Delete `writeLastContext` and its import and mock. Add a `projectOnboardingUrl(context)` helper in `lib/context.ts`, and use it here and in `HomeScreen.tsx:83` if that is convenient. One small behavior change: the last context is written after the navigation lands, not before it starts.

### 4. `inviteFailure` models a success as a failure and keeps a fallback the API cannot trigger
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/invite/inviteOutcome.ts:15, web/mobile/src/features/invite/inviteOutcome.ts:31, web/mobile/src/features/invite/useInviteAccept.ts:75-80
- What is wrong: `INVITE_ALREADY_ACCEPTED` is an ordinary success path, because OSS consumes the invite at sign-up. It still returns an `InviteFailure` with `retryable: false`, and the caller then has to branch on `alreadyAccepted` and never reads the other field. The `code === undefined && status === 409` branch is a copy from the old page. The accept handler in `organization_router.py:311-336` always sends a code with its 409, so the branch is a compatibility net for an API that no longer exists.
- Smallest fix: Delete the bare 409 branch and its test line. Check `isInviteAlreadyAccepted(error)` in the catch block, or return a small tagged result, so that `InviteFailure` only has `message` and `retryable`. Separately, the design says every string comes from the old page, but "Try again" is not in `web/oss/src/pages/workspaces/accept.tsx` or in `web/oss/src/components/pages/auth`. Confirm that string with the owner or take it from wherever it was copied.

### 5. The invited mark could be a value on the pending mark
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/onboardingPending.ts:6-7, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/onboardingPending.ts:48-62, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:62
- What is wrong: The invited key only has meaning while the pending key exists, and the code removes them together, so the two keys describe one fact. Nothing reads the value of the pending key today, only whether it exists. A second key gives a state that the code must avoid, which is why the host guards `invited` with `!preview`.
- Smallest fix: Keep one key. Write the value `"invited"` in `markOnboardingInvited`, and compare that value in `isOnboardingInvited`. The second `removeItem` goes away, and `invited` no longer needs the `!preview` guard. A mark is still needed, because the person can leave and come back through Home. This is optional.

### 6. The end of the question flow is inferred from `to === from`, and the deleted draft comes back
- Severity: Low
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:152-160, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/onboardingRoute.ts (`nextStep`), web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlowHost.tsx:189-192, web/mobile/src/features/onboarding/useDraftSave.ts
- What is wrong: `nextStep` returns the same step at the end of the list. Before this change no question could reach that case, and now that return value is the signal for "finished". `advance` has one caller, so the two-argument shape adds a step for the reader. Also, `reportCompleted` dispatches and then `onQuestionsDone` calls `endOnboarding` in the same tick. The dispatch commits after that, `useDraftSave` queues the new draft, and the timer or the unmount flush writes it back. So the answers stay in localStorage after `endOnboarding` deleted them. I found this by reading the code and did not run it. The effect is small, because the pending mark is gone and only the preview page would read that draft.
- Smallest fix: Have `nextStep` return `undefined` at the end of the list, and branch on that in the question's `onAdvance`. For the draft, the simplest choice is to accept the leftover and say so in a comment. Otherwise give `useDraftSave` a `discard` function that drops the pending save, and call it on this path.

## What to keep

- `ContextResolver` as the single reader of the pending invite. Every sign-in path ends at the root, so this avoids three places to keep in step.
- The localStorage invite with a 30 minute window, written through the existing `onInvite` callback. It has the same shape as `?template=`, and two short copies are cheaper than a shared storage helper for two callers.
- The questions-only path in the existing onboarding flow. The `steps` prop was already there, so filtering it reuses the step guards, the draft, and the analytics, including the `survey sent` check that follows the last shown question. A separate questions screen would copy all of that. The host still loads templates and the model for steps it does not show, and I do not think that is worth another branch.
- Opening onboarding directly from the accept screen. Home dismisses the pending mark when the project has agents, so going through Home would lose the questions in that case.
- `InvitedLinkDialog` as its own small component, and the thin `InviteAcceptScreen` and page shell.
- The one-line API link change.

Rating: Medium
